clue.text: Hung up and returned clothes not having right smell

indicators.note: returned means everything that follows is read backwards, clothes and smell together
not having tells us to take a letter out of the clothes word

parts.note: dresses are clothes
BO is body odour, a bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone fussily sends back garments because they don't smell right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the whole string DESSESBO, so the smell ends up at the front; 'Hung up' is the idiom for fixated, not hanging laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hung up on something is an idiom for being fixated or preoccupied with it.

clue.text: Subordinate to shout half-heartedly

indicators.note: half-heartedly says to lose half of the doubled middle letters, the heart of the shout word

parts.note: to bellow is to shout

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a junior a muted yell.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLOW has LL at its heart; 'half-heartedly' removes one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking beneath someone or under their authority is a synonym for being subordinate to them.

clue.text: Ravel composed ten new pieces, keeping only the second

indicators.note: composed means put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered
keeping only the second letter of the word pieces, its I

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel writing ten new pieces of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the composer, which 'composed' encourages, but it is the verb. The second letter of 'pieces' is I, which joins TEN NEW in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or twist threads together, the same as twisting them round one another.

clue.text: Misspell a word thus from Scotland to England?

indicators.note: to misspell is to get the letters in the wrong order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spelling lesson on how a word should be written in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland lies to the north of England, so going from one to the other is a direction of travel; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from Scotland to England means heading down the map, towards the south.

clue.text: Arrange crooked match payment

parts.note: to do something can mean to arrange it, as in doing the flowers
wry means twisted or crooked

explanation.surface: Someone fixing a bent sporting match and paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is a marriage, not a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's family traditionally handed over property or money at a wedding, a payment for the marriage match.

clue.text: Lectured about conclusion of special issue

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the lecturing word goes round a letter

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or lecture

indicators.note: conclusion of means the final letter of special

explanation.surface: A speaker talked about the end of a special edition of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a magazine number but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means offspring, so a son or daughter is someone's issue.

clue.text: Atmosphere cut short victory on board

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to clip is to cut
mate, checkmate, is victory on a chess board

explanation.surface: The mood after a narrow win on board ship was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the chessboard, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The prevailing mood or feeling in a place, as in a political climate, is its atmosphere.

clue.text: Playing tennis with writer's consuming a lot of resources

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around in play, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the writer says I've, short for I have, as writer's means writer has

explanation.surface: Playing tennis with a writer takes a lot of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' is read as 'writer has', the setter's I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour-intensive or energy-intensive work uses up a great deal of input.

clue.text: Contest where participants beat seven bells out of each other?

definitions.text: Contest where participants beat seven bells out of each other?

parts.words: Contest where participants beat seven bells out of each other?
parts.note: to knock seven bells out of someone is to beat them up; bells also ring with a ding and a dong, so a hard-fought struggle is pictured as bells ringing

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'beat seven bells out of' means thrash, and the answer's first half imitates bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiercely fought contest with the lead swinging back and forth is called this, after alternating bell chimes.

clue.text: Consider report of a suitable way of making money?

parts.note: to count someone lucky is to consider them so

indicators.note: report of means we hear the words spoken rather than read them

parts.note: a fitting thing is a suitable one

explanation.surface: Thinking about an account of an appropriate way to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a fitting' comes out as 'er-feiting'. The question mark flags that the money is made illegally, by forging.
explanation.definitionFit: Forging banknotes literally makes money, a punning description of the crime.

clue.text: One of the youngest Members of Parliament?

definitions.text: One of the youngest Members of Parliament?

parts.words: One of the youngest Members of Parliament?
parts.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so its youngest member is a baby owl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' is the collective noun for owls, not Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of the owl family belongs to the flock known as a parliament.

clue.text: Understood article in French documentary

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
documentary evidence is written down

explanation.surface: A French piece about a documentary film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'documentary' is the adjective, as in documentary evidence, not a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An understood rule or agreement is tacit, never set down on paper.

clue.text: Those recently acquainted with capital reportedly recognised half of London borough

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard spoken, so we use its sound

parts.note: knew means recognised

indicators.note: half of means only the first four of the borough's eight letters are kept

parts.note: Richmond upon Thames is a borough of London

explanation.surface: Someone is recognised in part of a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW said aloud sounds like NEW. RICHMOND is a borough in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have only lately come into wealth are newly familiar with money, the nouveaux riches.

clue.text: Felt desire made dogs start to yelp

indicators.note: dogs means follows closely behind, so the earning word comes after the letter
start to means the first letter of yelp

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone longed for something, which set dogs yelping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' is the verb 'follows', not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To long or pine for something is to feel a strong desire for it.

clue.text: The best low-calorie drug apparently

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
lite is a marketing spelling for low-calorie products

explanation.surface: The finest diet version of a drug, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The top group of anything, the cream or pick of the bunch, is the best of it.

clue.text: One officer not involved in dishonesty or breaking in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not involved in means the officer is taken out of the dishonesty word

parts.note: corruption is dishonesty
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: One police officer free of corruption or burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forcible entry, as of an army into territory, is a bursting in.

clue.text: Build-up about invention making a leap forward

indicators.note: making a leap forward means one letter jumps towards the front of the assembled letters

parts.note: C is circa, about
a creation is an invention

explanation.surface: A gradual build-up around an invention that is a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: C and CREATION give CCREATION; the A leaps to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual accumulation of layers or material over time is a build-up.

clue.text: Behaviour of gold and silver is optimal

definitions.note: the definition is a description: silver is the best metal for carrying electricity

parts.note: conduct is behaviour
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A claim about how precious metals perform, silver doing best.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: silver is the best electrical metal of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of any metal, making it the optimal carrier of current.

clue.text: Taboo representing attempt to reject everything but Christianity ultimately

parts.note: for means representing, as in an MP for a constituency
a bid is an attempt

indicators.note: everything but means all of the rejecting word except one letter

parts.note: to deny is to reject

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Christianity

explanation.surface: A forbidden topic that rejects every faith except Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: DENY loses its Y, the last letter of 'Christianity', leaving DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by custom or rule is banned, the sense of taboo.

clue.text: Foreign aid sent as an alternative

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so these letters come out in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Overseas aid was dispatched in place of something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one thing in place of another means choosing it as a substitute.

clue.text: Bed-wetting's not half upset this idiot

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are shaken into a new order
not half means only the first half of the hyphenated word is used

explanation.surface: A schoolyard taunt: this fool is distraught about wetting the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of BEDWETTING is BEDWE, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is slang for a boring, socially awkward person, a fool or nerd.

clue.text: Perhaps dispels Arsenal's charms

definitions.meaning: removing weapons from someone gets rid of their arsenal; perhaps marks the playful sense
to win someone over and dispel hostility is to charm them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a football club's appeal fades.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, but here an arsenal is a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking away weapons dispels an arsenal, and a winning manner likewise overcomes hostility.

clue.text: Translation of poems in papers set as a task

indicators.note: in means the reordered poems go inside the papers

parts.note: ID, identity papers

indicators.note: a translation changes the form of words, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Translating poems in newspapers was given as homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid down as an obligation or burden on someone has been imposed upon them.

clue.text: Knocked back having managed to invade Denmark's borders

indicators.note: to invade means to get inside, so the managing word goes in
borders means the outside letters of Denmark

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: An invading force got past the Danish frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking slang, not a military repulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back a drink is slang for swallowing it quickly.

clue.text: Jerk at university is leading one in class of 12

indicators.note: is leading means the university word goes in front

parts.note: being up is being in residence at university
a start is a sudden jerk

explanation.surface: A twit at college tops the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like the definition but is the wordplay; the definition points to 12 Across, the nouveaux riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has risen suddenly in wealth or rank is a parvenu, one of the nouveaux riches.

clue.text: Way of expressing interest about part on stage

parts.note: APR, annual percentage rate, is how loan interest is expressed
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: An actor showing interest in a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' is a section of the stage, not a role.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the section of stage jutting out in front of the curtain is called this.

clue.text: Rambling point one preceded with tirade

indicators.note: preceded means the numeral goes before the point

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tine is a point on a fork or antler
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A rambling speaker's argument precedes a furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering from place to place is travelling about, roving or roaming.

clue.text: Religious leader defaced painting of the country

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of religious
defaced means losing the front, its face, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a mural is a wall painting

explanation.surface: A priest has spoiled a landscape painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' is read literally: the face, the first letter, is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the countryside rather than towns is pastoral, rustic.

clue.text: Try and broadcast seed in this

parts.note: a go is a try
N stands for and, as in rock 'n' roll
an ad is a broadcast advertisement

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt sowing seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast seed' looks like sowing, but 'broadcast' is an advert and 'seed' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A testis or ovary is the reproductive organ where sperm or eggs are made.

clue.text: Fuel smoke rose near house

indicators.note: house is a verb here: the words contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Smoke rising near a building points to burning fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a building but is a verb meaning contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin, burned in lamps and jet engines, is a petroleum fuel.
